title: Edge-docked AI usage meter widget on a gradient phone wallpaper
contains_third_party_content: Icons inside the rings resemble AI-assistant brand logos; not confirmed.

color.method: Pixel sampling via median-cut quantization of the supplied JPEG/GIF (compressed images, so values are approximate within a few units). Entries marked 'approx' were judged by eye, not sampled.
color.roles: Soft, grainy rainbow gradient wallpaper; the widget is pure black with white text and three ring colors (orange-red, green, yellow; not precisely sampled).

observed.layout: Two phone corners at an angle on a dotted light background. A black vertical widget hugs the right screen edge, joined by inverted (concave) curves at top and bottom. It shows 3 circular progress rings with a logo each and percentages (73%, 21%, 52%), and a gear button at the bottom. Status bar shows 'Thu 29 Aug 11.22'.
observed.hierarchy: Black widget has the highest contrast on the page; rings are color-coded per tool.
observed.materials: Flat black with grain on the wallpaper; the widget's curves look like it grows out of the bezel.
observed.background: Grainy gradient wallpaper over a dotted off-white page.

interpretation.aesthetic: Ambient dashboard widget; brutally simple black element against an expressive gradient.
implementation_notes: Concave joins are CSS masks with radial gradients or SVG clip paths.
Rings: SVG circle with stroke-dasharray, or conic-gradient.
Persistent overlay on top of other apps is OS-dependent and may not be possible on all platforms; as a web/app widget it would sit inside the app only.
interpretation.caveat: Platform feasibility is Claude's assessment, not a creator statement.

concept_work.essence: Show the one number you care about (remaining usage) as a glanceable edge dock instead of an app you have to open.
what_makes_it_work: Extreme contrast separates it from any wallpaper.
Rings plus percentages give two readable encodings.
The edge position limits how much of the screen it takes.
gaps_to_make_it_work: System-level persistence is a feasibility question.
It overlays content and may block edge gestures.
Color alone distinguishes tools; labels are needed for accessibility.

lessons: A concept can be mostly an information decision: pick the single number to surface.
Check platform constraints before committing to overlay-style ideas.
open_questions: Which platform is it intended for?
